title: {{NAME}} and the Prehistoric Scouting Report
moral: The best analysis combines what the data says with what the heart knows.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a steel-blue soccer jersey with a gear emblem, grey shorts, and silver-blue cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
SCOUT-7 was the most advanced football analysis robot {{NAME}} had ever built.

It could track twenty-two players simultaneously, calculate passing probability in real time, and predict shot accuracy to within three degrees.

What it had never done was observe a Pterosaur playing football.

The Pterosaur arrived during the qualifying tournament via a temporal event, landed in the centre circle, picked up the ball with its feet, and flew it directly into the goal.

SCOUT-7 processed this for eleven seconds before saying: "I need to update my parameters."

pages.content:
The tournament rules, after considerable consultation, determined: aerial goals counted if the ball went in under the crossbar. The Pterosaur's natural flight ceiling was set as the offside line for aerial play.

{{NAME}} and SCOUT-7 spent the rest of the day updating parameters.

By evening, SCOUT-7 could track the Pterosaur's flight path, predict where it would redirect the ball, and calculate the optimal defensive positioning against it.

"How do you defend against a flying striker?" asked the tournament director.

"Three back, high line, tall defenders," said {{NAME}}. "SCOUT-7 will confirm."

pages.content:
The Pterosaur, it turned out, had specific weaknesses.

It struggled with low balls: its aerial precision was extraordinary but its ground game was limited by its wing structure.

{{NAME}} redesigned his team's strategy: keep the ball low, draw it to ground level, let SCOUT-7 signal the optimal moment to dispossess.

The Pterosaur's team scored three goals in the first half. {{NAME}}'s team scored four in the second, every one on the counter after forcing the Pterosaur to attempt ground play.

At the final whistle, the Pterosaur found this admirable in the way that athletes appreciate being genuinely beaten.

pages.content:
The temporal team arrived to return the Pterosaur after the match.

Before going through, the Pterosaur walked to {{NAME}} and SCOUT-7 and stood before them.

SCOUT-7 processed. "It appears to be regarding us as worthy opponents."

{{NAME}} nodded at the Pterosaur: the universal acknowledgement.

The Pterosaur blinked once. Then it walked through the portal.

"SCOUT-7," said {{NAME}}, "add Pterosaur aerial football to your standard parameters. Just in case."

"Already done," said SCOUT-7.

pages.content:
He put SCOUT-7 in its charging dock that night and sat at his desk reviewing the match data.

There was a three-second sequence at half time where SCOUT-7 had gone offline, overwhelmed by the unfamiliar variables, and he had made a tactical decision without it.

The right decision, as it turned out.

He thought about that.

Then he thought: SCOUT-7 is the best analysis tool he'd ever built. But the part that beats Pterosaurs is still him.

He turned off the light and went to sleep, satisfied.
